newsitem.title: USA: NYC to fight ending immigrants' benefits - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYC to fight ending immigrants' benefits - paper.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani plans to sue the federal government on Wednesday, charging that federal law's cutoff of benefits for legal immigrants is unconstitutional, the New York Times said.

In its Wednesday edition, the paper said the mayor's suit will argue that removing Food Stamps and cash benefits for elderly and disabled legal immigrants who are not citizens violates the due process clause of the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution. The suit seeks a permanent injunction against the parts of the new welfare and immigration laws that cut off the benefits.

The mayor's suit likely will be consolidated with separate suits to be filed by a coalition of public-interest legal organizations, including the Legal Aid Socieity, the Center for Constitutional Rights and the American Civil Liberties Union of Northern California, the paper said. They are expected to file class-action suits in Manhattan and San Francisco that also will challenge the laws.

New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani has cast himself as a national defender of the rights of immigrants. In October, he sued the federal government to block a provision in the laws that lets city employees turn in illegal immigrants who seek services like police protection, hospital care, and public education, the Times added.
